author: DamiLee
description:
The first thing I noticed on the MTR in Hong Kong was the colours. A lot of the older stations each have their own and I found out it was partly practical. In the 70s, many people in Hong Kong couldn't read, so you could spot your stop by its colour.

The MTR doesn't just run trains; it builds the flats and malls above and around the stations too. The property pays for the railway, and the railway pushes up the property values. The government still owns about 75% of it and, for years, fares alone brought in almost double what it cost to run.

What colour would the station for your home be and why?

#HongKong #MTR #PublicTransport #UrbanDesign #Architecture
title: Hong Kong Built the Trains First, Then the City
